answer: Unrepeatable challenge seeding. Each new identity must solve a challenge derived from live environmental entropy—say, a gale-driven sensor feed—so answers cannot be precomputed or reused. Registering also requires committing a distinct physical substrate token, like a numbered shale sample, whose origin is logged in a public grove of provenance records. An attacker must acquire and verify one unique substrate per identity, making mass registration cost real procurement plus verification time, not just cheap computation.
